decisions.why: A fix to the landing's refusal message, which makes the landing tooling report what blocks it. It keeps the refusal and narrows nothing the request or spec asks for.

decisions.summary: An open builder handoff names the clone only when its text names the clone root as a whole path, its task is not being landed, its task is open in some tasks.md, and it was written in the last 24 h (HANDOFF_FRESH_S, a CONVENTION knob). A handoff is named only beside changes, never as a refusal on its own.
decisions.why: These conditions decide which pointer the refusal prints. They never decide whether a dirty clone is refused, because the changes alone decide that. The 24 h bound is measured 2026-11-25: 26 of 538 handoffs would otherwise be wrongly named, all 2 to 5 days old. Nothing in request.md or the spec asks for a handoff to be named, so the bound narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The same check runs again at the push step's start, before the ticks; a refusal there ticks and pushes nothing.
decisions.why: Extends the refusal to the window between the claims wait and the ticks. It adds a refusal and carves nothing out.

decisions.summary: The tick's git add and git commit are read (commit_tick). A commit refused for index.lock is retried 3 times, 500 ms apart (CONVENTION knobs). On a failure the ticks are put back by unstaging and a checkout from HEAD, archives removed, fix rows set pending again, and the tick's escape record committed. Nothing is left staged.
decisions.why: Fixes the measured defect: an unread commit left the tick staged and sent the revert at the wrong commit. The undo is a checkout and never a history rewrite, which follows CLAUDE.md. The cause of the commit failure is left as a hypothesis, but the fix reads every failure, so the cause does not limit what it covers.

decisions.summary: After a failed push the revert always names the tick's own commit. Where another writer's edit blocks that revert, the tick commit stands, committed and never staged, with the existing message.
decisions.why: Corrects the revert's target. When the revert is blocked, the tick is left committed and stated, which is the outcome the plan's goal names ('committed or put back'). No defect is left: nothing is staged and the message says what happened.

decisions.summary: A clone dirty at make land's start still lands alone (451 T88/T101): alone_owed is asked before the first pass, and the new refusal is not placed before it.
decisions.why: Keeps earlier approved behavior that this task was not asked to change. It is not an exception to anything this task or the request asks for.

decisions.summary: The claims wait (CLAIMS_WAIT_S, 20 min) keeps waiting rather than refusing; check (2) covers the seconds after it.
decisions.why: Leaves an existing, pinned behavior as it is, with a stated reason (the claims round's records are committed beside the gate). Nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: A builder's linked worktree with uncommitted work, and a handoff naming that worktree, bear on nothing; such a landing lands (pinned).
decisions.why: A worktree's files and index are not in the clone's git status, so the rule's own subject (another writer in the tree the landing ticks in) does not include them. This states the rule's reach and carves no case out of it.
